questions.q: What is a prompt injection attack, as described in this lesson?
options: Instructions hidden inside content an agent reads (a document, a tool output), written to look like data but aimed at overriding the agent's task
A user directly asking the model to ignore its safety training in their own chat message
A SQL injection attack against a Snowflake table
A denial-of-service attack against a virtual warehouse
questions.explain: Prompt injection hides malicious instructions inside content the agent is told to trust, like a document returned by Cortex Search — not in the user's own prompt.

questions.q: How is a jailbreak different from a prompt injection, per this lesson?
options: A jailbreak is the user's own prompt trying to talk the model out of its safety behavior directly, rather than hiding the attack inside a document
A jailbreak only targets Cortex Search, never Cortex Agents
They are the exact same attack with two different names
A jailbreak only happens during fine-tuning, never at inference time
questions.explain: Jailbreak attempts come from the user's own message trying to bypass safety behavior directly, distinct from injection attacks hidden in external content.

questions.q: What is the always-on security baseline's job, versus Cortex AI Guardrails?
options: The baseline covers known injection techniques automatically; Guardrails is the opt-in layer using a specialized LLM to catch zero-day-style, previously-unseen attacks
The baseline only works on Cortex Analyst; Guardrails only works on Cortex Search
They do the exact same job, and Guardrails is just a renamed version of the baseline
The baseline is paid; Guardrails is free
questions.explain: Snowflake runs defense in depth: an always-on pattern-matching baseline for known techniques, plus an opt-in Guardrails layer using contextual reasoning for novel, zero-day-style attacks.

questions.q: Why does Cortex AI Guardrails run in parallel with the agent loop instead of as a blocking pre-check?
options: So it adds no noticeable latency to agent responses, reducing the chance teams disable it under deadline pressure
Because parallel execution is required by Snowflake's SLA
Because blocking checks are technically impossible in Cortex
So it can run on a different warehouse than the agent
questions.explain: A security layer that visibly slows every agent response risks being disabled by teams under pressure — running in parallel avoids that tradeoff.

questions.q: What does enabling Cortex AI Guardrails via ALTER ACCOUNT require?
options: Enterprise Edition and cross-region inference enabled
Standard Edition only, with no other prerequisites
A separate Cortex Search service already deployed
Disabling all row access policies on the account
questions.explain: The documented prerequisites are Enterprise Edition and cross-region inference (CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION set appropriately for the region).
